classification.difficultyReason: Combines graphical interpretation, binomial mean and standard deviation, an interval shading task and a reflected distribution.

content.prompt: A relative-frequency polygon is shown for the binomial distribution with $n=48$ and $p=0.25$.

spec.description: Editable binomial relative-frequency polygon, with horizontal grid step 3 and vertical grid step 0.025. Source magenta axes are ordinary graph furniture and use black under house style.
spec.answerVisibility: Always visible; writable stimulus for part d.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Is the distribution skewed to the left, skewed to the right or not at all?

answer.worked: Since $p=0.25<0.5$, the distribution is skewed to the right, as shown by its longer right tail.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the mean and standard deviation for the distribution.

children.label: c
children.prompt: What is the mode of the distribution? Estimate the probability of this most likely outcome.

answer.worked:
The peak occurs at $x=12$, so the mode is $12$. From the graph, $P(X=12)\approx0.13$.

This agrees with the binomial calculation:
$$\begin{aligned}P(X=12)&=\binom{48}{12}(0.25)^{12}(0.75)^{36}\\&\approx0.13.\end{aligned}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Shade the region no more than two standard deviations from the mean.

answer.short: Shade the region under the polygon for $6\le x\le18$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}\mu-2\sigma&=12-2(3)=6\\\mu+2\sigma&=12+2(3)=18\end{aligned}$$
Shade the region under the given polygon between $x=6$ and $x=18$, inclusive.

spec.sourceRegion: Part d and its supplied interval answer
spec.description: Complete solution graph with the region from 6 to 18 shaded light blue. Shading represents the requested two-standard-deviation interval.

children.label: e
children.prompt: Use the given sketch for $p=0.25$ to assist in sketching the graph of the distribution for $p=0.75$.

answer.short: Reflect the given polygon in $x=24$. The new polygon peaks at $x=36$, at about $0.13$, and is skewed to the left.
answer.worked:
The $p=0.75$ distribution counts failures in the original experiment. If the original number of successes is $k$, the number of failures is $48-k$.

Thus each point $(k,P(X=k))$ moves to $(48-k,P(X=k))$. The graph has the same shape reflected in $x=24$, with mode $36$ and a longer left tail. This also follows from $\binom{48}{k}=\binom{48}{48-k}$.

The horizontal mapping $k\mapsto48-k$ can be obtained by shifting left by $48$, then reflecting in the $y$-axis. Reflection in a line $x=a$ is not required syllabus knowledge here.

spec.sourceRegion: Supplied blue answer graph below part e
spec.description: Binomial relative-frequency polygon for p=0.75, reflected from the supplied p=0.25 polygon. Blue identifies the answer series; ordinary axes and tick labels use black.
spec.mathematics: P(Y=k)=P(X=48-k) for X~Bin(48,0.25), Y~Bin(48,0.75). Mode 36, peak approximately 0.1319843.
